title: Borreguil · Wet Meadow Finder — finding and mapping borreguiles (high-mountain wet meadows)
description: Desktop application for the automatic identification of borreguiles (high-mountain wet meadows) using multi-source remote sensing and machine learning. It combines Sentinel-2 time series (vegetation, moisture and water indices), Sentinel-1 radar, topographic variables derived from the Copernicus digital elevation model (elevation, slope and curvature) and texture descriptors from high-resolution orthophotography. A Random Forest classifier, trained on 769 verified points in Sierra Nevada (Spain; 372 borreguiles and 397 non-borreguiles) and validated with spatial cross-validation by river catchment, estimates the probability that each point is a borreguil. With the reviewed points, it also trains a model for the study area, validates it by zones and produces a 10 m borreguil map in Google Earth Engine. The program also includes a hierarchical classification of borreguil type (environment, moisture and pixel purity), automatic selection of the decision threshold and the option to retrain the model with local field data. It is distributed as a self-contained executable for Windows, macOS and Linux, with no need to install Python or any dependencies.
